quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the car straight and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed the same and steer straight.
Swerve side to side to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the car straight and slow down by lifting your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have control of the car. Once it is under control, brake gently and pull to a safe spot on the road.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always understand the dangers they face.
Cannot fully control their body, mind, or vehicle.
Drive better because they are more careful than sober drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot fully control their body, mind, or vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you see:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
A traffic officer ordering you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unfasten your seat belt and roll down your window.
Get your documents ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Ask passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to leave. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right only after making a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn right.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows rules drivers must follow. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: The best safety protection in a crash comes from:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best when used with seat belts. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belt.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your signal light.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal light three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Driving ability can be affected by:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and tiredness all make driving unsafe.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
When turning left on a green light, you must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning left on a green light, you must wait for oncoming traffic to pass.
questions.explanation: This sign with a traffic signal tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. You must wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning left.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time you drive.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object and hurt others in the car during a crash.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something back to the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and move out of the way. Trying to get even with an aggressive driver can make the situation worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants
questions.explanation: Everyone in a moving vehicle must wear a seat belt. Police can stop and ticket drivers or passengers not wearing one. If a passenger under 16 is not wearing a belt, the driver will be fined.

questions.question: To turn right, you should be in:

options.text: The lane closest to where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go, and turn into the lane closest to your current lane.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is ahead.

questions.question: Highway markings:
questions.correctAnswerText: Give information to drivers.
questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers know where to position their vehicles, show safe passing areas, and warn about upcoming conditions.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
Signal only if other traffic is visible.
Signal only in heavy night traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from the curb. Make this a habit every time.

questions.question: The most important thing when backing a car is to:

options.text: Look behind your vehicle and yield to others.
Keep one foot on the brake.
Keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look behind your vehicle and yield to others.
questions.explanation: Before backing, turn to look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors. Look left and right and yield to other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an incline than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles with sirens, air horns, or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: If you see side-by-side red lights flashing at a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and cross the railroad.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: If you see side-by-side flashing red lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before moving into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving.
